string-array.name: guide_steps_free
string-array.item: Pick a free source: Proton (sign-up → Downloads → WireGuard) or Cloudflare WARP via the wgcf tool.
Generate and download the .conf — no payment needed.
Prefer your own server? A permanent free VPS tier (Oracle Cloud Always Free) + wg-easy from the self-hosted section costs nothing.
Import into SecureNet: Servers → Import → file, QR or paste.

string-array.name: guide_steps_paid
string-array.item: Pick a provider with a config generator — every provider marked above.
Subscribe; most offer a 30-day money-back guarantee, so testing is risk-free.
In the dashboard open the WireGuard config generator, choose server and port, download the .conf.
Import into SecureNet and connect — keep the provider\'s file as a backup.

string-array.name: guide_steps_selfhosted
string-array.item: Get any small VPS (Oracle Cloud has a permanent free tier; Hetzner or DigitalOcean ~ $4/month).
Run one installer: wg-easy (Docker), PiVPN, Algo or the wireguard-install script.
Open UDP 51820 in the provider\'s firewall and download a .conf per device.
Import each profile into SecureNet — your own server, zero monthly fees.

string-array.name: guide_steps_routers
string-array.item: Open your router\'s admin panel (GL.iNet: VPN → WireGuard; OpenWrt: install luci-proto-wireguard).
Create a WireGuard server or client interface.
Add a client peer and export its .conf (or scan the QR code shown).
Import the profile into SecureNet so your phone carries the same tunnel anywhere.

string-array.name: guide_steps_apps
string-array.item: Install the official WireGuard client for your platform.
Import the provider\'s .conf or scan their QR inside the app.
Verify the handshake works outside SecureNet.
Re-import the same .conf into SecureNet for the full feature set: split tunneling, kill switch, multi-hop.

string-array.name: guide_tips
string-array.item: Treat a .conf like a password: it holds keys that identify your device — never share or post it.
Beware of random \"free WireGuard config\" lists on social media — whoever built the config can see and route your traffic.
No handshake? Re-check the endpoint port (try 51820, then 443) and confirm the server public key matches the provider\'s page.
Connected but no internet? The provider\'s DNS is usually missing — set DNS = 1.1.1.1 in the config.
Slow or unstable on mobile data? Lower MTU to 1280–1380; the optimizer screen can suggest a value.
One profile per device keeps keys unique — and a PresharedKey (when offered) adds another strong layer.
